claims.statement: For every finite ordinary connected tree T, with integer p=alpha(T)-2 and x(T) the first natural rank with Delta_x(T)<0, eligibility x(T)+2<=p implies alpha(T)>=7.
claims.scope: Exact auxiliary eligibility guard for finite ordinary connected trees under the semantic and solution contracts; no residual premise and no aggregate-sign conclusion.
claims.reason: The imported verified r27 arbitrary-rank forest lemma applies to the exact integer Delta_x and gives n<=4x. Eligibility plus a<n reduces alpha<=6 to alpha=6, x=2, n=7 or 8. The exact pair/triple count and one-/two-vertex cover bounds give Delta_2>=5 or >=2, contradicting strict descent. Independent finite checks corroborate the small cases and a 13-vertex eligible double star tests the larger setting.

limitations: The argument imports the r27 forest descent bound as verified historical authority; no new Lean build or formal gate was run in this critique.
The first-interior aggregate and the proposed tagged-shadow and high-tail pointwise statements remain unproved by this auxiliary guard.
The finite enumeration covers only labeled orders seven and eight; the proof itself excludes larger low-alpha contradiction cases by n<=4x<=8.
